original_card.question: Which unresolved physical correction, endpoint transport or hosting obligation in a pinned P104 follow-up can be closed or decisively rejected?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the P104 row in research-family-status.md and its exact pending source heads before choosing a task. #1991 is the reviewed channel; #2586 is a pending physical dual with explicit added transport costs, not an admitted supplier.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: Check live claims, pin the chosen follow-up and reproduce only the evidence needed for one unresolved obligation. Compare its complete correction/transport/hosting invoice with the target budget; test legal chronological access. Do not rebuild #1991 or assume #2586 has solved global admission.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.

existing_restriction_being_changed: Nothing is relaxed. The restriction being audited is PR 2717's demoted residue item (c): 'for non-dyadic entries (odd primes in denominators) the mod-2 anchor does not apply at all', together with the exact scope of Lemma AN's hypothesis ('after per-total powers of two the factorization is 2-integral') and Lemma MX's anchor premise. Every claim carries its exact status label; no 'exactly when' or necessity wording is used beyond the parts proved in both directions (Lemma SC's criterion and Lemma SG's reach).
method: Exact stdlib rational (fractions.Fraction) and F2 arithmetic. Lemma SC: the per-total contents c_j = min_t v_2(p_j(t)) + min_s v_2(q_j(s)), invariant under per-total rescaling; the factorization normalizes to 2-integral iff every c_j >= 0. Lemma SG: one global power-of-two rescaling by 2^{-gamma}, gamma = min_j c_j, makes every rational factorization of every entry class 2-integral; the mod-2 anchor then anchors exactly S_gamma = {t : v_2(M_tt) = gamma} and no power-of-two normalization anchors any other line. Pattern invariance: (pi, sigma, Z), cert(M) and every chain cost are invariant under global rescaling, so F-star's truth domain is entry-class-independent. Engine (signature/opts, exact-completion DP, independent witness checker, hill_climb/exact_cert, chain machinery, zero-digraph MAS/MP/chi) adapted from PR 2774 / PR 2747 / PR 2717 (Aaron Wang), which adapt DreamingOfClouds' PR 2111 model. New: the scope machinery above, the mixed anchor+pivot Lemma-MX values with A = S_gamma (both order forms, U = empty), and the entry-class generators evenden / oddden / mixed.

open_questions.question: Does the scale-invariant anchor reach |S_gamma| plus one-sided repairs always reach floor(2v/3)? Concretely: for every rank-3 decoder, is |{t : v_2(M_tt) = gamma}| plus the PR 2747 repairable count at least floor(2v/3)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would prove F-star for every entry class through the anchor route alone, with no zero-digraph hypothesis; the fixtures show the pure anchor is short (0/12 on tied_min), so the repairs or the pivots must carry the residue.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate tied-heavy decoders at v <= 8 with controlled gamma (force all diagonals above gamma, then one, then two lines at gamma) and test the anchor+repair count against floor(2v/3).
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing structural; needs a dedicated enumeration session.

open_questions.question: What is the maximum, over factorizations of a fixed decoder pattern, of the scale-invariant anchor reach |{t : v_2(M_tt) = gamma}|?
open_questions.why_it_matters: gamma and S_gamma depend on the chosen 3-total factorization; a GL_3(Q) re-split of the same M can change both. A characterization would sharpen Lemma SG from 'for every factorization' to a pattern-level bound.
open_questions.first_step: On tied_min and cex_min_1, sample GL_3(Z) re-splits of the stored factorization and track gamma and the reach; test whether the reach can exceed the recorded anchor_good counts without violating the recorded certificate limits 11/18.
